Slovakia vs Czechia

2026 (see official game summary)
IIHF Ice Hockey World Championship 2026
Slovakia (SVK) 2:3 Czechia (CZE)

Report generated from a manually reconciled IIHF shot-chart dataset. Official score, shots on goal and blocked shots are separated from transparent location-based proxy metrics. Chronological metrics are excluded because the source does not contain reliable event time or order.

Prepared by Antonin Kremenak

Executive summary

  • Slovakia controlled 52 of 99 validated attempts (53%) and 30 of 48 official shots on goal (62%).
  • The location-based model also favored Slovakia: 9–10 high-danger chances and 3.23–3.09 in Shot Quality Index.
  • Slovakia converted its territorial edge decisively in the third period, scoring 0 of its 2 goals in the final frame.

5. Advanced insider layer

The following metrics are proxy-based insider indicators built from the available shot-location sample. They are useful for storytelling, but they are not a substitute for full play-by-play or tracking data.

Metric legend

Percentages: share of all validated shot-chart attempts by the team. Spatial categories can overlap, so the columns are not expected to sum to 100%.

High danger / HDC: attempt within 25 feet of the goal and no more than 22 feet from the centre line.

Middle lane: attempt no more than 12 feet from the centre line.

Net front: attempt from the deep central area (at least 82 feet into the attacking direction and within 12 feet of the centre line).

Slot: attempt from the inner-slot area (68–92 feet into the attacking direction and within 18 feet of the centre line).

Perimeter: attempt at least 22 feet from the centre line or from the point side of the offensive zone.

Point shots: attempts taken less than 45 feet into the attacking direction.

Validated SOG: goals plus saved shots in the manually reviewed shot-chart dataset.

Chances: all medium- and high-danger attempts. HDC includes only high-danger attempts.

SQI: Shot Quality Index, a location proxy weighted 0.18 / 0.07 / 0.02 for high / medium / low-danger attempts; it is not a trained expected-goals model.

Goals / …: goals divided by the named denominator. Goals / SQI is a descriptive finishing proxy, not an xG-overperformance estimate.

  • Czechia had the strongest danger-oriented shot style: perimeter / point-shot oriented.
  • Slovakia generated the clearest central-access pattern: strong central-lane access.
  • Czechia had the highest goals-per-SQI finishing efficiency and roughly aligned with chance quality.
  • Spatial metrics use validated shot coordinates. Sequence, pressure, rebound and score-state metrics stay disabled until chronological play-by-play is available.

7. Validation, methodology and sources

Publication validation

Team Goals Shots on goal Blocked shots Validated attempts Validated Fenwick Status
SVK 2 / 2 30 / 30 13 / 13 52 39 OK
CZE 3 / 3 18 / 18 13 / 13 47 34 OK
  • Official inputs: final score, shots on goal and blocked shots.
  • Validated shot-chart inputs: player number, shot result and spatial coordinates for all plotted attempts.
  • Proxy metrics: scoring chances, high-danger chances, Shot Quality Index and style classifications are transparent rules based on shot location; they are not an official tracking feed or a trained expected-goals model.
  • Intentionally excluded: momentum, rebounds, pressure windows and score-state behavior require chronological play-by-play data that the IIHF shot chart does not contain.
  • Source documents: game_summary.pdf, shots.pdf and lineups.pdf from the IIHF match report package.
  • Official competition source: https://www.iihf.com/en/events/2026/wm/schedule
